To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the density structure of the Rosette cloud is filamentary; 2) the density distribution of the cloud has a non log normal shape; 3) the non log normality is caused by shock compression; 4) the density structure is the same in the UV exposed and the shielded parts of the cloud; 5) the density structure does not differ between low and high mass forming regions.
star formation in the Rossette molecular cloud is triggered by the formation of filaments in the turbulent cloud, and that clusters form at the junctions between filaments.
star formation in high mass star-forming clouds is not globally triggered but occurs locally at the junctions between filaments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether star formation is triggered by UV radiation or not.
the formation of clusters in the Rosette cloud, a high mass star forming region.
the formation of molecular clouds and star formation in the context of the turbulent interstellar medium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
star formation is not triggered by UV radiation but by the turbulent structure of the molecular cloud.
star formation is not triggered by the OB cluster but that it is a natural process in the cloud.
star formation in molecular clouds is not triggered by UV radiation but by turbulence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

star formation in the Rosrote molecular cloud is not globally triggered but locally by expanding HII regions, but that it takes place in filamentary structures that arose from the turbulent structure built up in the formation of the whole cloud.
high mass star formation is not a special case, but rather a consequence of the turbulent nature of molecular clouds.
the Rosette cloud shows a hierarchical structure of star formation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the star formation in the Rosettes molecular cloud is a result of the complex interaction between the turbulence and gravity, and not a result of the feedback from the massive stars in the NGC 2244 OB cluster.
feedback from OB stars has no impact on the large scale structure of the Rosette molecular complex and the global star forming process.
star formation is a local process that is triggered by the compression of the filaments, and not by the global UV impact.
